settlements.name: Roma
settlements.description: The capital of the Roman Republic and Empire.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Capua
settlements.description: An important ancient city of Campania with Villanovan and Etruscan origins.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Tibur
settlements.description: A Sabine town, 30 km east-north-east of Rome, Tibur was the seat of the Tiburtine Sibyl.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Praeneste
settlements.description: An ancient city of central Italy, the eighth and seventh century B.C. origins of which demonstrate high-level trade contact with the Eastern Mediterranean world. The city withdrew from the Latin League (499 B.C.) and opposed Rome in the Latin war; Cincinnatus eventually subdued Praeneste. Sulla founded a new colony there in the first century B.C.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Norba
settlements.description: Norba, located in the Monti Lepini, was a member of the Latin League (ca. 499 B.C.) and became a Latin colony ca. 492 B.C. The city was destroyed in the early first century B.C.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Tarracina
settlements.description: A strategic Volscian city that had come under Roman control by 509 B.C.; a Roman citizen colony was established there in 329 B.C. The site is particularly notable for the remains of the terraced sanctuary of Iuppiter Anxur.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Ostia
settlements.description: The port city of ancient Rome located at the mouth of the river Tiber.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Antium
settlements.description: Antium ranked as one of the most important and most powerful centers of Latium and was captured by Rome at the close of the Latin War in the fourth century B.C. Imperial Antium was well known for its number of coastal villas.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Lanuvium
settlements.description: Lanuvium was an important city of Latium located south of the Alban Hills. After opposing Rome at the battles of Aricia (504 B.C.) and Lake Regillus (496 B.C.), Lanuvium was captured by the Romans in 338 B.C.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Aricia
settlements.description: Aricia was an ancient Latin settlement and a member of the Latin League.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Anagnia
settlements.description: Anagnia was a Hernican town that sided with Rome against the Volscians and later became civitas sine suffragio. By Cicero's time it received the status of municipium.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Fregellae
settlements.description: Fregellae was a city of Latium Adiectum that became a Roman colony in 328 B.C., but was subsequently captured by the Samnites; a Roman presence was re-established in 313 B.C. Loyal to Rome during the Second Punic War, Fregellae revolted in 125 B.C., and the site was razed.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Arpinum
settlements.description: An ancient center that originated as early as the seventh century B.C., which became a civitas sine suffragio in 305 B.C. Arpinum was the birthplace of Caius Marius and Marcus Tullius Cicero.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Setia
settlements.description: A Volscian settlement of the fifth century B.C. that became a Latin colony in 382 B.C.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Formiae
settlements.description: An ancient settlement of likely Greek origin along the Via Appia. Cicero was assassinated near Formiae (now Formia) in 43 B.C.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Minturnae
settlements.description: Originally an Ausonian town that fought against Rome in 314 B.C., Minturnae became a colony in 296 B.C. The site is located on the Garigliano river (ancient Liris) and served an important economic function. The Via Appia passes through the city.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Kyme
settlements.description: An ancient settlement of Campania, Cumae was the first Greek colony established on the Italian mainland in the eighth century BC.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Neapolis
settlements.description: Founded as Parthenope by Greeks in the eighth century B.C., the site eventually gave rise to Neapolis in the sixth century B.C. and was one of the most prominent cities of Magna Graecia. Present-day Naples, Italy.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Nola
settlements.description: The city of Nola (Nuvlana) is considered one of the oldest in Campania. Under Augustus, the settlement became a Roman colony; it was the spot where Augustus died in A.D. 14.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Pompeii
settlements.description: An ancient city of Campania destroyed by the volcanic eruption of Mt. Vesuvius in A.D. 79, Pompeii was named as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Maleventum
settlements.description: Beneventum/Maleventum (modern Benevento) was an ancient city of Campania of Samnite origin.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Poseidonia
settlements.description: Greeks from Sybaris originally founded Poseidonia/Paestum, a major Greco-Roman center of south Italy, in the seventh-century BCE. It was originally named Poseidonia. After the Pyrrhic war, the city became a Latin colony named Paestum ca. 273 BCE.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately

settlements.name: Diana at Nemi
settlements.description: A site sacred to Diana near Lake Nemi, comprised of a Tuscan-style sanctuary and a sacred grove.
settlements.precision: gazetteer representative point; period suitability reviewed separately
